study_design: Nested case-control study within the prospective Health Professionals Follow-up Study
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We matched 450 incident prostate cancer cases diagnosed from 1993-1998 to 450 controls by age, time, month, and year of blood donation.
reason: This prospective nested case-control analysis evaluated overall incident prostate cancer diagnosis and did not report an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Modest inverse, but not statistically significant, associations were observed among plasma alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, and lycopene concentrations, and overall risk of prostate cancer diagnosis [odds ratio (highest versus lowest quintile; OR), alpha-carotene: OR, 0.67 [95% confidence interval (CI), -0.40-1.09]; beta-carotene: OR, 0.78 (95% CI, 0.48-1.25); lycopene: OR, 0.66 (95% CI, 0.38-1.13)].
estimate_classifications.reason: The lycopene estimate is explicitly for overall risk of prostate cancer diagnosis.
